title: Elena R. Maren v. Aster Quay Logistics, Inc.
jurisdiction_basis: 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331, 1291; Title VII retaliation; final judgment disposing of sole claim; represented private parties

timeline.description: Maren starts as dispatch coordinator at Oakland facility.
Release policy revision distributed to dispatch and shift leads.
Customer raises complaint about consignment AQ-4470, handled by Bellford.
Holtwell requests common audit of six coordinators.
Maren emails HR complaint about sex-based allocation of lead shifts.
Bracken tells Holtwell of the nature of the complaint and instructs preservation.
Holtwell requests expanded lookback for Maren.
Maren interviewed with HR; identifies oral approvals and log defects.
Fenmore sends correction note; eight of twelve flags resolved, four remain, two disputed authorization.
Holtwell proposes termination; HR seeks comparator information.
Holtwell issues written warning to Bellford.
COO reviews recommendation and HR packet.
Summary judgment hearing; no live testimony.
Order and separate final judgment entered.

facts.value: documented approval; oral approval allowed for qualifying urgent loads; record before shift end

issues.question: Whether the summary judgment record permits a reasonable jury to find that the protected opposition was a but-for cause of discharge, considering the audit chronology, comparator and disciplinary process.
issues.standard_of_review: de novo; reasonable inferences for nonmovant
issues.preservation_status: raised in opposition; exact pages to be checked after drafting
issues.ruling_quote: The motion for summary judgment is granted.
issues.preservation_quote: A reasonable jury could find that the protected complaint was a but-for cause of discharge.
issues.appellant_theory: Cumulative evidence of selective investigation, disputed explanations and comparator treatment permits inference of but-for causation.
issues.appellee_theory: Precomplaint audit and documented release violations justified the same discharge; distinctions and incomplete logs do not permit a causal inference.
issues.appellant_relief: Vacate judgment and remand for trial.
